transcript.text: Hi, I've got a Dyson V15 Detect (SV22) about 4 months old. When I go from the kitchen tiles onto the lounge rug the motor suddenly gets much louder and the battery number drops faster, then it calms down again when I go back on the tiles. Also the screen goes up and down by itself. Is the motor on its way out? It's still under guarantee so I want to report it before it dies completely.

Switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. To answer your question: it is unlikely that the motor is failing. However, the screen flickering or changing readings by itself suggests a potential issue with the dust sensor or the display unit. Before you claim it under guarantee, please try this: ensure the vacuum is in 'Auto' mode (not Boost), and gently wipe the small sensor window on the floorhead with a dry cloth to remove any dust that might be confusing it. If the screen continues to fluctuate erratically when you are just moving over tiles or if the suction doesn't seem to adjust logically, please contact Dyson support directly as this may require a warranty repair.

It's already showing 'Auto' on the screen, so I haven't got it on Boost. I'm not sure which sensor window you mean on the floorhead, though, and I don't want to poke at anything. There's no burning smell, heat or sparks, and no warning lights or red on the screen, if that helps.

The motor getting louder on the rug is normal behaviour for a vacuum in Auto mode as it detects more debris (or reflects off the carpet fibres) and ramps up power, which also explains the faster battery drain. However, the screen going 'up and down by itself' when you are just moving between surfaces is not normal. Because your V15 Detect is only 4 months old and still under guarantee, I recommend contacting Dyson Support directly to arrange a warranty repair for the sensor/display unit.

Thank you. Just so I understand: you're saying the motor getting louder on the rug is normal in Auto mode, but you think the screen changing is a fault? The runtime number and the particle graphic only change while I'm cleaning, and I'm not sure the screen is actually faulty. Should I still contact Dyson, or is this all just how Auto mode works?

To answer your question directly: no, this is not all just how Auto mode works. While it is completely normal for the motor to get louder and drain the battery faster on rugs (as the vacuum detects resistance/debris), the screen changing readings by itself when you are simply moving between surfaces is a fault. It suggests the laser dust sensor or the display unit is malfunctioning. Since your V15 Detect is only 4 months old and still under guarantee, you should contact Dyson Support to arrange a warranty repair for this specific issue.
